intro.title: Safe area insets
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage header that adapts its padding to avoid overlapping with device notches or rounded corners. You will learn the core concept of safe area insets, which are CSS environment variables that provide dynamic spacing for modern device screens. The main technologies involved are the CSS `env()` function and the `safe-area-inset-*` variables. This will help you create designs that look great on all devices, from phones to tablets, by automatically adjusting for their unique screen shapes.
intro.usecase: Safe area insets are essential for creating mobile-friendly interfaces that adapt to device-specific features like notches, rounded corners, and home indicators. You'll use them in mobile apps and responsive websites to ensure content like navigation bars, bottom menus, and full-screen modals doesn't get obscured by these hardware elements. For example, in a mobile banking app, you'd apply safe area insets to keep transaction buttons and account balances visible on devices with notches, while in an e-commerce app, you'd use them to prevent product images from being clipped by rounded screen corners. This technique ensures your UI remains functional and visually consistent across all modern mobile devices.
